mainTopic: The value of the צבור and the בית הכנסת: praying with the congregation, places of learning, and conduct around קריאת התורה.
overview: The amud opens with the power of praying with the צבור. The time when the congregation prays is an 'עת רצון', and God does not reject the prayer of the many. ריש לקיש warns that someone who has a shul in his city but does not go in is a 'שכן רע'. רבי יוחנן learns that people in בבל live long because they come early and stay late in shul. רב חסדא says to go in the distance of two doorways before praying. Then the גמרא lists several readings of 'לעת מצא': a wife, תורה, death, burial and the bathroom, and in ארץ ישראל they preferred מר זוטרא's bathroom reading. Back on the shul, רב חסדא and עולא teach that ה׳ loves places of הלכה learning most, so אביי, רבי אמי and רבי אסי davened where they learned. עולא also praises one who lives from his own work and advises living near one's רב, if the student listens to him. The amud ends with rules about the Torah reading: not walking out on the ספר תורה, and reading the weekly פרשה twice with the תרגום once.

steps.title: A time of favor is when the congregation prays
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the פסוק 'ואני תפלתי לך ה׳ עת רצון' to mean that the best time to pray is when the צבור is praying.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the פסוק mean, 'But as for me, my prayer is to You, ה׳, at a time of favor'? When is a time of favor? At the time when the congregation is praying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'a time of favor' in a פסוק means and answers that it is when the צבור prays together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says there is a special 'עת רצון', a time when prayer is welcomed more. The גמרא tells us when that time is: whenever the צבור is davening together. So a person who prays with the צבור is praying at that favored time.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of that which is written (a formula that opens an explanation of a פסוק)
A time of favor, when God accepts prayer
The congregation, a community praying together

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source in this סוגיא for the special value of davening with a צבור.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of that which is written:
"But as for me, my prayer is to You, ה׳, at a time of favor"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 69:14

phrases.english: When is a time of favor?
At the time when the congregation is praying.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the power of praying with the צבור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'עת רצון' of the פסוק is the time when the צבור prays.

steps.title: A second source from ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא brings a different פסוק, from ישעיהו, to teach the same idea about the צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: we learn it from here: 'Thus says ה׳: at a time of favor I answered you.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives his own פסוק as the source that prayer at a 'time of favor' is answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is the same as in the first step, but the source is different. Here the 'עת רצון' is found in a פסוק where God Himself promises 'I answered you.' That shows that prayer at this special time really is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: From here (I learn it from this פסוק)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: we learn it from here:
"Thus says ה׳:
At a time of favor I answered you."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 49:8

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק as the source for the same idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God promises to answer prayer offered at an 'עת רצון', the time of communal prayer.

steps.title: A third source: God does not reject the many
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא ברבי חנינא combines a פסוק in איוב with a פסוק in תהלים to show that God does not reject the prayer of a group.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא ברבי חנינא said: we learn it from here: 'Behold, God does not despise the mighty,' and it is written: 'He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle against me, for many were with me.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא brings two פסוקים together as yet another source for the power of praying with the צבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says God 'does not despise' the כביר, which is read as a large group of people. The second פסוק says David was saved 'because many were with me.' Together they show that God does not turn away a prayer said with many people.

keyTerms.meaning: Mighty or great; here read as 'the many'
And it is written (bringing a second פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: Read on its own, 'הן אל כביר ולא ימאס' could mean 'God is mighty and despises no one.' Here it is read as 'God does not despise the mighty,' meaning a large group.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַחָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Aḥa, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: we learn it from here:
"Behold, God does not despise the mighty"
phrases.notes: איוב 36:5. Here כביר is read as 'the many,' so God doesn't turn away a big group.

phrases.english: And it is written:
"He redeemed my soul in peace
from the battle against me,
for many were with me."
phrases.notes: תהלים 55:19

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַחָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, different source for the same idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God does not reject the prayer of the many; prayer with many people brings salvation.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי אחא's source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי נתן uses the same two פסוקים as רבי אחא to prove that God does not reject the prayer of the many.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא. רבי נתן says: from where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not despise the prayer of the many? As it says: 'Behold, God does not despise the mighty,' and it is written: 'He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle against me,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that an earlier source, a ברייתא, already used the same פסוקים as רבי אחא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תניא נמי הכי' means a תנא said the same thing. So רבי אחא's reading is not just his own idea. רבי נתן, a תנא, already joined these two פסוקים to teach that God accepts communal prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (support for what was just said)
And so on (the rest of the פסוק)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Natan says:
From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not
despise the prayer of the many?
As it says: "Behold, God does not despise the mighty,"

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״פָּדָה בְשָׁלוֹם נַפְשִׁי מִקְּרָב לִי״ וְגוֹ׳,
phrases.english: and it is written: "He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle against me," and so on.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the source of רבי אחא from step 3 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אחא ברבי חנינא's reading of the two פסוקים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי נתן that uses the same two פסוקים.

steps.title: Torah, kindness and communal prayer redeem God and His children
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on to read the פסוק as God's own words. Whoever learns תורה, does גמילות חסדים and prays with the צבור is treated as if he redeemed God and His children from the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Holy One, Blessed be He, says: anyone who is busy with תורה and with acts of kindness, and who prays with the congregation, I consider it for him as if he redeemed Me and My children from among the nations of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן explains the פסוק 'פדה בשלום נפשי' as God speaking, and lists three deeds that bring this huge reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the 'my soul' in the פסוק is read as God's 'soul,' not David's. The three deeds are learning תורה, doing גמילות חסדים and davening with the צבור. They are so great that God credits the person as if he redeemed God and the Jewish people from גלות among the nations.

keyTerms.meaning: I credit him, I consider it for him

steps.whatToRemember: Davening with the צבור is an 'עת רצון', because God does not reject the prayer of the many. Joined with תורה and גמילות חסדים, it is counted as redeeming God and His children.
steps.whyThisMatters: This raises davening with a צבור from a nice practice to something with huge spiritual weight. That is why it is pushed so strongly in practice.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, says:
Anyone who is busy with Torah
and with acts of kindness,
and prays with the congregation,
I consider it for him
as if he redeemed Me, Me and My children,
phrases.notes: God is the speaker here, so 'my soul' in the פסוק means God Himself.

phrases.english: from among the nations of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי נתן's ברייתא, explaining the פסוק as God's words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who learns תורה, does גמילות חסדים and prays with the צבור is credited as if he redeemed God and His children from the nations.

steps.title: Someone who skips the shul in his city is called a bad neighbor
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that a person who has a בית הכנסת in his city but does not go in to pray is called a 'שכן רע' (bad neighbor), based on a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Anyone who has a בית הכנסת in his city and does not go in there to pray is called a 'bad neighbor,' as it says: 'So says ה׳ about all My bad neighbors who touch the inheritance that I gave to My people ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש adds a new statement about תפילה with the צבור. He gives a harsh name to someone who has a shul nearby but does not use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1-5 praised praying with the צבור. Now the גמרא looks at the other side: what is wrong with someone who stays away. The פסוק talks about neighbors who only 'touch' God's inheritance, meaning they are close to it but never go in.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת בְּעִירוֹ,
phrases.english: Anyone who has a synagogue in his city
and does not go in there to pray
is called "a bad neighbor,"
as it says: "So says ה׳
about all My bad neighbors
who touch the inheritance
phrases.notes: He only 'touches' the shul by living near it, but he never actually goes in.

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר הִנְחַלְתִּי אֶת עַמִּי אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל״.
phrases.english: that I gave as an inheritance to My people, Israel."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 12:14

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כָּל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת בְּעִירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from praising those who pray with the צבור to criticizing someone who has a shul nearby and stays away.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who has a בית הכנסת in his city and does not enter to pray is called a שכן רע.

steps.title: He also brings exile on himself and his children
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש adds that such a person also causes גלות for himself and his children, based on the rest of the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but he brings exile on himself and his children, as it says: 'Behold, I will uproot them from their land, and I will uproot the house of יהודה from among them.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש continues his statement and adds a second, heavier punishment. He gets it from the end of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 gave the person a bad name. This step adds a real result: being uprooted from the land, for him and also for his children. Both ideas come from one פסוק in ירמיהו.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but... (adds something more)

phrases.english: And not only that, but
he brings exile on himself and his children,
as it says: "Behold, I will uproot them from their land,
and the house of Judah I will uproot from among them."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁגּוֹרֵם גָּלוּת לוֹ וּלְבָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues ריש לקיש's statement and adds the punishment of גלות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who avoids the בית הכנסת causes גלות for himself and his children.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is surprised that people in בבל live long
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יוחנן hears that there are old people in בבל, he is amazed. The תורה promises long life 'on the land,' which seems to mean only in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told רבי יוחנן: There are old people in בבל. He was amazed and said: It is written, 'So that your days and the days of your children will be many on the land.' But outside the Land, not!?
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins. רבי יוחנן finds it hard to understand how people outside ארץ ישראל can live long lives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads 'on the land' as limiting the promise of long life to ארץ ישראל. So long lives in בבל seem to go against the פסוק. This difficulty sets up the answer in the next step.

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Yochanan:
There are old people in Bavel.
He was amazed and said:
"So that your days will be many
and the days of your children on the land" is written,
phrases.notes: דברים 11:21. 'The land' here means ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: but outside the Land, not!?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּמַהּ וַאֲמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story that will connect long life to going to the בית הכנסת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that people in בבל live long lives
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק promises long life 'on the land' (ארץ ישראל), which suggests there is no such blessing outside the Land.

steps.title: Coming early and staying late in shul is what helps them
steps.stepSummary: Once רבי יוחנן hears that the people of בבל come early and stay late at the בית הכנסת, he says this is what gives them long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they told him that they come early and stay late at the בית הכנסת, he said: That is what helps them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן's surprise is answered. Their long life comes from their dedication to the בית הכנסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The promise in the פסוק is about the land, but there is another way to earn long life: coming to shul early and staying late. So long lives in בבל do not go against the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: They come early (in the morning) and stay late (into the evening)

steps.whatToRemember: Going early and staying late at the בית הכנסת can bring long life, even outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Once they told him
that they come early and stay late at the synagogue,
he said: That is what helps them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ מְקַדְּמִי וּמְחַשְּׁכִי לְבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבי יוחנן's surprise from step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Long life comes only from living in ארץ ישראל, so people in בבל should not live long.
steps.terutzMaskana: Coming early and staying late at the בית הכנסת also brings long life, so it works for them even in בבל.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives his sons the same advice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רבי יוחנן's answer with the advice רבי יהושע בן לוי gave his sons: come early and stay late in shul so that you will live long.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יהושע בן לוי said to his sons: Come early and stay late and go into the בית הכנסת, so that your lives will be long.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the idea from step 9 with another אמורא who taught the same thing to his children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דאמר' (as he said) shows this is support for the previous step. רבי יהושע בן לוי directly connects coming early and staying late in shul with long life.

keyTerms.meaning: That your life will be long

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לִבְנֵיהּ:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said to his sons:
Come early and stay late
and go into the synagogue,
so that your lives will be long.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לִבְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 9 with a matching teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That coming early and staying late at the בית הכנסת brings long life
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's advice to his sons

steps.title: The verse behind long life for those who come to shul
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא ברבי חנינא gives the source in משלי: happy is the one who watches at God's doors every day, and right after it says that whoever finds God finds life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא ברבי חנינא said: What is the verse? 'Happy is the person who listens to Me, to watch at My doors every day, to guard the doorposts of My entrances.' And it is written right after it: 'For one who finds Me finds life.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אחא ברבי חנינא shows where in תנ״ך the idea comes from, that coming to God's 'doors' brings long life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק describes someone who comes to God's doors every day, which fits coming to shul. The very next פסוק promises 'life' as the reward. So the two פסוקים together link going to shul with long life.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (asking for the source)
And it is written right after it

steps.whatToRemember: The source is משלי: one who comes daily to God's doors 'finds life.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha son of Rabbi Chanina said:
What is the verse?
"Happy is the person who listens to Me,
to watch at My doors every day,
to guard the doorposts of My entrances,"
phrases.notes: משלי 8:34

phrases.english: and it is written right after it:
"For one who finds Me finds life."
phrases.notes: משלי 8:35

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רבי יהושע בן לוי's advice.
steps.raayaObject: That going to the בית הכנסת regularly brings long life

steps.title: רב חסדא: go two doorways into the shul
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that a person should always go 'two doorways' into the בית הכנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: A person should always go two doorways into the בית הכנסת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a practical rule about entering the shul. His wording is unclear, and the גמרא is about to question it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the next move. Read literally, it sounds like a person must pass through two separate doors, which the גמרא will find hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: Always (a general rule of good conduct)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A person should always go in
two doorways into the synagogue.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לְעוֹלָם יִכָּנֵס אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical rule about entering the shul, after the פסוק about God's doors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should go 'two doorways' into the בית הכנסת.

steps.title: Can it really mean two actual doorways?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the literal reading: could רב חסדא really mean a person must pass through two doorways?
steps.simpleTranslation: Two doorways? Could you really think that?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the plain meaning of רב חסדא's words. It sets up a new explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'סלקא דעתך' means 'could it enter your mind?' The גמרא finds the literal reading, walking through two separate doors, impossible to accept as רב חסדא's meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (this cannot be right)

phrases.english: Two doorways, could you really think that?!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי פְתָחִים סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of רב חסדא in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal wording 'two doorways' in רב חסדא's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes no sense to require passing through two actual doors to enter a shul.

steps.title: It means the distance of two doorways, then pray
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב חסדא meant a person should go into the shul a distance equal to two doorways, and only then pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: the distance of two doorways, and then he should pray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading רב חסדא's words as a measure of distance, not a number of doors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Two doorways' is a measurement: walk in about the width of two doorways before starting to pray. This way a person does not stand at the entrance, but truly comes inside.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (read it this way instead)

steps.whatToRemember: Don't pray right at the entrance of the shul. Go in about the distance of two doorways first.
steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not saying a shul needs two doors or that you must pass through two doors. 'Two doorways' is a measurement of how far inside to go.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
the distance of two doorways,
and only then should he pray.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא, שִׁיעוּר שְׁנֵי פְתָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13 by reinterpreting רב חסדא's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא meant going through two actual doorways.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant going in the distance of two doorways before praying.

steps.title: The 'time of finding' is finding a wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that 'לעת מצא' in תהלים refers to finding a wife, based on the פסוק 'he who finds a wife finds good.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'For this, let every pious person pray to You at a time of finding.' רבי חנינא said: 'a time of finding' means a wife, as it says: 'He who found a wife found good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from תהלים about praying 'at a time of finding,' and רבי חנינא says the thing being found is a wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מצא' (find) is the link. In משלי, the same word is used for finding a wife ('מצא אשה'). So רבי חנינא reads the תהלים פסוק as saying a חסיד should pray to find a good wife.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק as proof)

phrases.english: "For this, let every pious person pray
to You at a time of finding"
phrases.notes: תהלים 32:6

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
"At a time of finding": this is a wife
as it is said: "He who found a wife found good."
phrases.notes: משלי 18:22

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: ״לְעֵת מְצֹא״ זוֹ אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps 11 to 14 dealt with going to shul and the פסוק 'whoever finds Me finds life.' Now the גמרא moves to another פסוק built on the word 'finding.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לעת מצא' means a person should pray to find a good wife.

steps.title: The groom's question in ארץ ישראל: מצא or מוצא?
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל, people would ask a new groom 'מצא or מוצא?', meaning: does your wife fit the good פסוק in משלי or the bitter פסוק in קהלת?
steps.simpleTranslation: In ארץ ישראל, when a man married a woman, they would ask him: 'מצא or מוצא?' 'מצא', as it is written: 'He who found a wife found good and obtained favor from ה׳‎.' 'מוצא', as it is written: 'And I find the woman more bitter than death.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a custom from ארץ ישראל that shows how strongly 'finding' was tied to marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two פסוקים about a wife that use the word 'find.' One uses the past tense 'מצא' and praises the wife. The other uses the present tense 'מוצא' and calls the woman bitter. Asking the groom 'מצא or מוצא?' was a short way of asking which פסוק describes his marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: The West, meaning ארץ ישראל (west of בבל)
Found (past tense), from the good פסוק in משלי
Finds (present tense), from the bitter פסוק in קהלת
Short for 'וגומר': 'and so on,' the rest of the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: The two words sound almost the same, but they point to two opposite פסוקים. מצא is the good one (משלי). מוצא is the bitter one (קהלת).

phrases.english: In the West
phrases.notes: The 'West' is ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל.

"Motzei," as it is written:
"And I find more bitter than death
the woman," and so on.
phrases.notes: קהלת 7:26

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי חנינא's link between 'finding' and a wife by showing a real custom that used the same פסוק.

steps.raayaSupportSource: The custom in ארץ ישראל of asking a groom 'מצא or מוצא?'

steps.title: רבי נתן: the 'time of finding' is תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן disagrees and says 'לעת מצא' refers to finding תורה, based on 'whoever finds Me finds life.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: 'a time of finding' means תורה, as it says: 'For whoever finds Me finds life.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion: רבי נתן says the thing a חסיד should pray to find is תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof פסוק in משלי is spoken by wisdom, which חז"ל understand as תורה, and it uses the word 'find.' So for רבי נתן, the most important thing to pray to 'find' is תורה, which brings life.

keyTerms.meaning: תורה, the thing to be 'found' in רבי נתן's view

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
"At a time of finding": this is Torah,
as it is said: "For whoever finds Me finds life," and so on.
phrases.notes: משלי 8:35, the same פסוק quoted back in step 11.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: ״לְעֵת מְצֹא״ — זוֹ תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different meaning of 'לעת מצא' than רבי חנינא's 'wife.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לעת מצא' means a person should pray to find תורה.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the 'time of finding' is death
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says 'לעת מצא' refers to death, based on the פסוק 'לַמָּוֶת תּוֹצָאוֹת.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: 'a time of finding' means death, as it says: 'The ways out to death.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the 'time of finding' is the time of a person's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof rests on a similar-sounding word: 'תוצאות' (ways out) sounds like 'מצא.' Since that פסוק links the word to death, he reads 'לעת מצא' as the time of death, when a person should pray to leave the world peacefully.
steps.whatToRemember: Three meanings of 'לעת מצא': רבי חנינא says a wife, רבי נתן says תורה, and רב נחמן בר יצחק says death.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
"At a time of finding": this is death,
as it is said: "The ways out to death."
phrases.notes: תהלים 68:21. תוצאות sounds like מצא, and that sound link is the proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר — ״לְעֵת מְצֹא״ זוֹ מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third meaning of 'לעת מצא,' different from both a wife and תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לעת מצא' means a person should pray about the time of his death, that it be peaceful.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports reading the verse as death: 903 kinds of death
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא backs up רב נחמן בר יצחק. It says 903 kinds of death were created, because the word תוצאות adds up to 903. The hardest death is אסכרא and the easiest is נשיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: 903 kinds of death were created in the world, as it says 'לַמָּוֶת תּוֹצָאוֹת'. The letters of 'תוצאות' add up to that number. The hardest of them all is croup (אסכרא), and the easiest of them all is the 'kiss' (נשיקה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the last opinion, רב נחמן בר יצחק's view that 'לעת מצא' means death. It uses the same פסוק he used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק based his view on the word תוצאות. The ברייתא adds that this word equals 903 in גימטריא, so there are 903 ways to die. This fits his idea: a person should pray to die an easy death and not a painful one.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way. This introduces a ברייתא that supports what was just said.
The number value of the letters in a word
Croup, a painful throat disease. It is the hardest kind of death.
The 'kiss' of death. It is the gentlest kind of death.

as it says: "Issues of death,"

phrases.notes: ת is 400, ו is 6, צ is 90, א is 1, ו is 6 and ת is 400. Together that makes 903.

steps.title: What the hardest and easiest deaths feel like
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא describes אסכרא with a picture of a thorn caught in wool. Some say it is like ropes stuck in the throat. נשיקה is like pulling a hair out of milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Croup is like a thorn caught in a clump of wool that gets pulled out backwards. Some say it is like ropes at the opening of the throat. The 'kiss' is like pulling a hair out of milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains, using pictures from everyday life, how painful אסכרא is and how gentle נשיקה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a thorn caught in wool is pulled out backwards, it rips the wool apart. That shows how hard the soul's leaving is with אסכרא. A hair comes out of milk with no effort at all, and that is what נשיקה is like.

phrases.english: Croup is like a thorn
in a clump of wool
that is pulled out backwards,
phrases.notes: Pulling it out backwards rips up the wool on the way out.

phrases.english: and some say:

The kiss is like

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two kinds of death named in step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אסכרא is extremely painful, while נשיקה is effortless

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the 'time of finding' is burial
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives another explanation: 'לעת מצא' means burial. A person should pray to be buried properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: 'At the time of finding' means burial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another explanation of 'לעת מצא'. רבי יוחנן says it means burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list of explanations continues: a wife, תורה, death, and now burial. On this reading, the time a person should pray for is getting a proper burial.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
"At the time of finding" — this is burial.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לעת מצא' refers to burial

steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: What is the פסוק for this? 'Who rejoice to the point of exultation, and are glad when they find a grave.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives a source for רבי יוחנן's view: a פסוק where people 'find' a grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is יִמְצְאוּ (they find), which links to מְצֹא in 'לעת מצא'. Since the תנ"ך speaks of 'finding' a grave, it makes sense that 'the time of finding' means burial.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק? This asks for the verse that is the source.

"Who rejoice to the point of exultation

phrases.notes: איוב 3:22

steps.title: A common saying: pray until the very last shovelful
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא connects this to a popular saying: a person should keep praying for mercy right up until the last shovel of dirt on his grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא said: This is what people mean when they say: A person should ask for mercy even until the last shovelful of dirt, so that it goes peacefully.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב שילא shows that a well-known saying expresses the same idea as רבי יוחנן: even burial is something to pray about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Prayer is needed even after death, all the way until the grave is closed. So a respectful, peaceful burial is a real 'time' to pray for, which fits reading 'לעת מצא' as burial.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: the 'time of finding' is the bathroom
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא gives a very down-to-earth explanation: 'לעת מצא' means finding a בית הכסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: 'At the time of finding' means the bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more explanation. מר זוטרא says 'לעת מצא' means finding a bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back then, finding a decent place to relieve oneself was not easy. So even this basic need is something a person should pray for.

"At the time of finding" — this is the bathroom.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל they prefer מר זוטרא's explanation
steps.stepSummary: The scholars in ארץ ישראל say that מר זוטרא's explanation is the best of all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say in the West (ארץ ישראל): This explanation of מר זוטרא is better than all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the list by telling us which explanation the scholars of ארץ ישראל liked best: מר זוטרא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After five different explanations (a wife, תורה, death, burial and the bathroom), this line ranks them and picks מר זוטרא's as the best. It doesn't say why. It only reports that ארץ ישראל preferred it.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: 'לעת מצא' has many explanations: a wife, תורה, death, burial and the bathroom. In ארץ ישראל they held מר זוטרא's bathroom explanation was the best.
steps.confusionAlert: Being called the 'best' does not cancel the other explanations. The גמרא is only saying which reading the scholars of ארץ ישראל preferred.

steps.title: רבא asks to hear רב חסדא's teachings about the shul
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רפרם בר פפא to share the excellent teachings he said in the name of רב חסדא about the בית הכנסת. This brings the גמרא back to its main topic.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רפרם בר פפא: Let the master tell us some of those excellent teachings that you said in the name of רב חסדא about matters of the shul.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next part. The side discussion is over, and רבא's request opens a new set of teachings about the בית הכנסת, which רפרם will now share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse explanations started as a side topic. This request steers the גמרא back to its main subject, prayer and the shul. The answers come in the steps that follow.

steps.title: רב חסדא: ה׳ loves the gates distinguished in הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רפרם בר פפא answers רבא by quoting רב חסדא's explanation of the פסוק 'אהב ה׳ שערי ציון‎': ה׳ loves places distinguished in הלכה more than בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם said to him: This is what רב חסדא said. What does the פסוק mean, 'ה׳ loves the gates of ציון more than all the dwellings of יעקב'? ה׳ loves the gates that are distinguished in הלכה more than shuls and study halls.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם answers רבא's request from the last step by sharing one of רב חסדא's teachings about the בית הכנסת. רב חסדא reads a פסוק in תהלים as praising places of הלכה learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא reads the word ציון as if it were מצוינים, meaning 'distinguished.' So 'שערי ציון' means gates that stand out because הלכה is learned there. The 'dwellings of יעקב' are the regular בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות, which are holy, but the places of הלכה learning are loved even more.

steps.title: עולא: after the חורבן, ה׳ has only the ארבע אמות של הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רב חסדא with עולא's teaching that since the בית המקדש was destroyed, ה׳'s place in His world is only the ארבע אמות של הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this matches what רבי חייא בר אמי said in the name of עולא: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, the Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world except the ארבע אמות של הלכה alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching that says the same idea as רב חסדא. It shows how special places of הלכה learning are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא says that after the חורבן, the place where ה׳'s presence is found in the world is the 'ארבע אמות' where הלכה is learned. This explains why רב חסדא said places of הלכה are loved even more than shuls. In a way, these places have taken over the role of the בית המקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a matching teaching that supports רב חסדא's idea from step 27.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's teaching that places of הלכה learning are loved most
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא's statement that after the חורבן‎, ה׳ has only the ארבע אמות של הלכה

steps.title: אביי starts davening where he learns
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports that he used to learn at home and daven in shul, but after hearing עולא's teaching, he davened only where he learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: At first I would learn at home and daven in the shul. Once I heard what רבי חייא בר אמי said in the name of עולא, that from the day the בית המקדש was destroyed ה׳ has nothing in His world except the ארבע אמות של הלכה alone, I would only daven in the place where I learned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows a practical result of עולא's teaching. אביי changed where he davened because of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, אביי split his day: learning at home, davening in shul. Once he heard that ה׳'s presence is found in the place of הלכה learning, he decided to daven there too. So the teaching was not only a nice idea. It changed real behavior.

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
At first I would learn inside the house
and daven in the shul.
Once I heard this

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא
phrases.english: that Rabbi Chiya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla
— "From the day the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ
phrases.english: the Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה בִּלְבַד
phrases.english: except the four amos of halacha alone"

phrases.aramaic: — לָא הֲוָה מְצַלֵּינָא אֶלָּא הֵיכָא דְּגָרֵיסְנָא.
phrases.english: — I would daven only in the place where I learned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה גָּרֵיסְנָא בְּגוֹ בֵּיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a practical way of acting on עולא's teaching from step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because ה׳'s presence is in the place of הלכה learning, אביי davened where he learned.

steps.title: רבי אמי and רבי אסי daven between the pillars where they learned
steps.stepSummary: Even with thirteen shuls in Tiberias, רבי אמי and רבי אסי davened only between the pillars of the place where they learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי, even though they had thirteen shuls in טבריא, would daven only between the pillars, in the place where they learned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another real-life example of the same practice. Two great אמוראים in ארץ ישראל davened where they learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'even though they had thirteen shuls' show they had plenty of choices. They still chose the place of their learning. This strengthens the point that the place of הלכה learning is the most special place to daven.

keyTerms.meaning: Tiberias, a city in ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא and עולא teach that the place of הלכה learning is the place most beloved to ה׳ after the חורבן. אביי, רבי אמי and רבי אסי acted on this by davening where they learned.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi,
even though they had
thirteen shuls in Tiberias,
would daven only between the pillars,
in the place where they would learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי אַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲווֹ לְהוּ תְּלֵיסַר בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא בִּטְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second practical example alongside אביי's in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: The practice of davening in the place of הלכה learning
steps.raayaSupportSource: The conduct of רבי אמי and רבי אסי in טבריא

steps.title: One who benefits from his hard work is greater than a God-fearing person
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אמי, in the name of עולא, teaches that one who lives from his own hard work is greater than a ירא שמים. He proves it from the extra words 'וטוב לך' in that person's פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אמי said in the name of עולא: A person who benefits from his own hard work is greater than a ירא שמים. About the ירא שמים it says 'Happy is the man who fears ה׳.' About the one who lives from his work it says 'When you eat from the work of your hands, you are happy and it is good for you.' 'You are happy' means in this world, and 'it is good for you' means in the World to Come. About the ירא שמים, 'it is good for you' is not written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from עולא, comparing a person who earns his own living with a ירא שמים. It proves that the worker is greater by comparing two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the word 'אשרי' (happy). Only the worker's פסוק adds 'וטוב לך', which the גמרא reads as a promise for עולם הבא. Because the worker gets that extra promise, he is called greater.

keyTerms.meaning: One who benefits from (lives off) his own hard work
You are happy (here read as reward in this world)
And it is good for you (here read as reward in the World to Come)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying that fear of Heaven is unimportant. The whole proof rests on one extra phrase, 'וטוב לך', that appears only in the worker's פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla:
Greater is one who benefits from his own hard work
than a God-fearing person,
for about a God-fearing person it is written:
"Happy is the man who fears ה׳,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 112:1

phrases.english: while about one who benefits from his hard work it is written:
"When you eat from the work of your hands,
you are happy and it is good for you."
phrases.notes: תהלים 128:2

phrases.english: "You are happy" means in this world,
"and it is good for you" means in the World to Come,
and about the God-fearing person,
"and it is good for you" is not written about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the teachings about where to daven, the גמרא adds another teaching from עולא on a new subject.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who benefits from his own hard work is greater than a ירא שמים, since only he is promised 'וטוב לך', reward in עולם הבא.

steps.title: A person should live where his teacher lives
steps.stepSummary: Also from עולא: a person should always live in the place of his רב. The proof is that שלמה did not marry בת פרעה as long as his teacher שמעי בן גרא was alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אמי said in the name of עולא: A person should always live in the place where his teacher lives. For as long as שמעי בן גרא was alive, שלמה did not marry בת פרעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from עולא: a student should live near his רב. It proves this from the story of שלמה המלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having a רב nearby keeps a person away from wrongdoing. While שלמה's teacher שמעי בן גרא was alive, שלמה did not marry בת פרעה. Only after שמעי died did that marriage happen.

keyTerms.meaning: Always (a word used to give general advice)
In the place of his teacher
שמעי son of גרא, known as שלמה's teacher

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla:
A person should always live in the place of his teacher,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁשִּׁמְעִי בֶּן גֵּרָא קַיָּים,
phrases.english: for as long as Shimi ben Gera was alive,
phrases.notes: The proof only works because שמעי בן גרא is understood to have been שלמה's teacher.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נָשָׂא שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה.
phrases.english: Shlomo did not marry Pharaoh's daughter.
phrases.notes: In מלכים א, the marriage is told right after שמעי's death (end of chapter 2, start of chapter 3).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא: לְעוֹלָם יָדוּר אָדָם בִּמְקוֹם רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching from the same chain (רבי חייא בר אמי quoting עולא), on a new subject.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should always live near his רב, because a teacher's presence protects from sin, as with שלמה and שמעי בן גרא.

steps.title: A ברייתא says not to live near one's teacher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא with a ברייתא that says a person should NOT live in his רב's place.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: he should not live there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא's teaching by quoting a ברייתא that seems to say the exact opposite. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said 'ידור', he should live near his רב. The ברייתא says 'אל ידור', he should not. These look like a direct contradiction.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: he should not live there!
phrases.notes: He means a ברייתא that says not to live in your teacher's place, the opposite of עולא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the teaching of step 32 with a ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that a person should always live in the place of his רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says 'אל ידור', directly opposite to עולא's 'ידור'.

steps.title: It depends on whether the student listens to his teacher
steps.stepSummary: Both are correct. Live near your רב if you listen to him; don't live near him if you don't.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. This one (live near him) is when the student submits to his רב. That one (don't live near him) is when he does not submit to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two sources are talking about two different kinds of students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's advice is for a student who listens and accepts his רב's guidance, so living nearby helps him. The ברייתא is for a student who does not listen. For him, living close to his רב would only lead to trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
This one... that one (splitting two cases)
He submits to him, listens to him

steps.whatToRemember: Living near your רב protects you from sin, but only if you actually listen to him. If you don't, it is better to live elsewhere.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
this is where he submits to him,
phrases.notes: 'This' is עולא's advice to live near the teacher.

phrases.english: that is where he does not submit to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דִּכְיִיף לֵיהּ, הָא דְּלָא כְּיִיף לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (הא בהא): the two sources talk about different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עולא and the ברייתא seemed to disagree about whether to live near one's רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Live near your רב if you listen to him; if you don't listen, don't live near him.

steps.title: Walking out on the Torah reading is like abandoning ה׳
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of רבנים, רבי אמי teaches that the פסוק 'those who forsake ה׳ will perish' is about a person who leaves the ספר תורה and walks out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said in the name of רבי מנחם, who said in the name of רבי אמי: What does the פסוק 'Those who forsake ה׳ will perish' mean? It is about a person who leaves the ספר תורה behind and walks out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the subject of shul and gives a new teaching. Walking out while the ספר תורה is being read counts as 'forsaking ה׳'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי takes a general פסוק about people who abandon ה׳ and applies it to a concrete case in shul. Getting up and leaving while the Torah is open looks like turning your back on ה׳. This sets the basic rule that the next steps will narrow down.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? This is how the גמרא opens an explanation of a פסוק.
One who leaves the ספר תורה behind

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the halacha that a person should not leave shul in the middle of קריאת התורה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said,
Rabbi Menachem said,
Rabbi Ami said:
What is meant by what is written: 'Those who forsake the Lord will perish'?
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:28

phrases.english: This is one who leaves the Torah scroll and goes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב, ״וְעוֹזְבֵי ה׳ יִכְלוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the general subject of shul from steps 30 and earlier, after the side topic about living near one's רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving the ספר תורה and walking out falls under 'עוזבי ה׳ יכלו'.

steps.title: רבי אבהו left only between one reader and the next
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רבי אבהו would leave during the pause between one person's reading and the next person's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו used to go out between one man and the next man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how a great רב actually behaved with this rule. רבי אבהו left only in the gap between two people's readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows רבי אמי's rule. Leaving while someone is in the middle of reading is forbidden, but the break between readers was not treated as abandoning the Torah. רבי אבהו's practice shows that a natural pause makes leaving acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: Between one man and the next man (between one person's reading and the next)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ נָפֵיק בֵּין גַּבְרָא לְגַבְרָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu would go out between man and man.
phrases.notes: 'Man and man' means the people called up to read. He left in the pause after one finished and before the next began.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ נָפֵיק בֵּין גַּבְרָא לְגַבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows an acceptable way to leave, which marks the edge of the ban from step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving in the break between one reader and the next is permitted, based on רבי אבהו's practice.

steps.title: What about leaving between one פסוק and the next?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether the small break between one פסוק and the next also counts as a pause where leaving is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: What is the law about leaving between one פסוק and the next?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks a follow-up question about רבי אבהו's practice. If leaving between readers is fine, is a smaller break between פסוקים also fine?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Between readers there is a clear stop. Between פסוקים the reading is still going on with only a short break. So the question is whether any pause is enough, or only the full break between readers.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question, not an attack)
Between one פסוק and the next

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
Between verse and verse, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: בֵּין פְּסוּקָא לִפְסוּקָא מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי אבהו's practice and asks whether a smaller pause works the same way.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the break between one פסוק and the next enough of a pause to allow leaving shul?

steps.title: The question is left unanswered
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found to רב פפא's question, so it ends in תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question stands unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without answering רב פפא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תיקו' means the question stays open. We know leaving between readers is allowed, but we don't know whether leaving between פסוקים is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question stays unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: Walking out while the ספר תורה is being read is called 'forsaking ה׳'. Leaving between one reader and the next is fine, as רבי אבהו did. Leaving between one פסוק and the next is an open question (תיקו).
steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is 'yes' or 'no'. It means the גמרא never decided the question.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב פפא's question without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether one may leave between one פסוק and the next stays unresolved.

steps.title: רב ששת turns away to learn during the reading
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת would turn his face away during קריאת התורה and learn. He explained that he was busy with his Torah learning, and the צבור was busy with theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת would turn his face away and learn. He said: We are busy with ours, and they are busy with theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רב ששת, who turned away from the ספר תורה during the reading and kept learning. It also gives his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 35 said that someone who walks out on the ספר תורה is included in 'those who forsake ה׳ will perish.' רב ששת's behavior looks like a problem at first. His answer shows he was not leaving Torah at all: he was learning Torah himself, so he does not count as one who forsakes ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: Learns, studies (literally 'grinds,' going over the material)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב ששת was ignoring the Torah reading out of disrespect. His point is that he was also busy with Torah, so he is not like the person who walks out on the ספר תורה.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet would turn his face away
phrases.notes: He means turning away from the ספר תורה while it was being read.

phrases.english: and study.
He said: We are with ours,
phrases.notes: 'Ours' is his own learning. 'Theirs' is the צבור listening to the reading.

phrases.english: and they are with theirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מַהְדַּר אַפֵּיהּ וְגָרֵיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further case to the discussion of leaving during קריאת התורה. רב ששת's case is allowed because he was busy with Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who turns away from the reading to learn Torah himself is not considered one who forsakes ה׳.

steps.title: Always finish the weekly portion with the congregation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי teaches that a person should always complete the weekly פרשה along with the צבור. He should read the text twice and the תרגום once.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said in the name of רבי אמי: A person should always finish his portions together with the congregation, reading the text twice and the translation once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching of רבי אמי. Each week a person should go through the same פרשה the צבור is reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves from how to act during the public reading to a personal duty. Each person must read the weekly פרשה himself, keeping pace with the צבור. The method is fixed: the פסוקים twice and the Aramaic תרגום once.

keyTerms.meaning: Always, a strong instruction for how a person should act
His Torah portions, the weekly פרשה
The written text of the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The source for the well-known practice of שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום: each week, read the פרשה twice in the original and once in תרגום, together with the צבור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source for the practical הלכה of reading שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום every week.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said,
Rabbi Ami said:
A person should always complete his portions
with the congregation.
phrases.notes: He means keeping pace with the פרשה being read in shul that week.

phrases.english: Twice the text,
and once the translation.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם יַשְׁלִים אָדָם פָּרָשִׁיּוֹתָיו עִם הַצִּבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching connected by topic (Torah reading with the צבור). It is not an answer to the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must complete the weekly פרשה along with the צבור: the text twice and the תרגום once.
